verification.note: Confirmed by reading the code. VideoPlayer.src.test.tsx:265 and :300 check only `not.toContain(0)`. Every call to `write` in playbackProgress.ts is behind `usable()` (value > 0): :105 (notifyEnded), :191-193 (tick) and :269-275 (teardown). So saveProgress can never receive 0, and the assertion cannot fail. In the first I3b test, the old controller's teardown runs after the new controller is handed out, because usePlaybackProgress's effect cleanup runs on the re-render with the new mc. It reads currentTime 30 from the reused <video> (set by keepCurrentTime at :244) and writes 30, and the assertion accepts that.

Confirmed. server-routes.test.ts:5-34 calls isStreamPath only on bare pathnames. The query stripping is at server.js:61 (`new URL(req.url, ...).pathname`) and the dispatch at server.js:72-73 (`backendProxy.web`). Grep finds no test under frontend/src that references server.js or backendProxy.

unspecified_scores.reason: It needs a caller that passes onError without src inside the iOS shell. The documented addon pattern (ADDON-DEVELOPMENT.md:1402-1404) always passes both, so this rarely happens, and when it does a playback error just isn't reported to the caller.
It needs an addon to swap src while the same video stays open, which is rare. The user then loses at most the last few seconds of resume position on the old source.
Only a first-party addon author's own bug passes a whitespace-only src, which is outside ordinary use. The player then shows a broken source instead of falling back.

specification_compliance: I1/I2: VideoPlayer.tsx:250 uses `src || getStreamUrl(videoId)`, and :330 picks ShellVideoPlayer only when inside the native shell and src is falsy.
I3b: the controller effect's dependencies include src (VideoPlayer.tsx:174), so a src change hands null and then a new controller to onMediaController.
I4: onError is bound only to the <video> element's onError (VideoPlayer.tsx:258), not to the <track> elements.
I5: the regex at server-routes.js:16 matches the declared pattern.
regression_risks: The I3b tests would not catch a regression that saves a stale or new-element position after a src change, because the assertion is vacuous (F1).
test_coverage: Tests cover I1/I2 rows inside and outside the shell, the I3 progress, controller, ended and artwork checks, I3c autoplay, I4 error and track events, and I5 pathnames.
Not covered: the I3 queue-page next/previous handlers with src, routing a query-bearing stream URL through server.js, and a meaningful 'no save before reseek' check for I3b.
not_verified: I did not run the test suite; all conclusions come from static reading.
I did not check real-browser currentTime reset behaviour on a src change.
I did not read backend/app/routers/addon_proxy.py or design-decisions.md.
